title: Routing is a measurable partition of task-space
html:
Statement. Let each task \(t\) carry a load vector \(\ell(t)=(\ell_M,\ell_T,\ell_P)\in\{0,1\}^3\), where \(\ell_M,\ell_T,\ell_P\) indicate nonzero load on the Memory, Tools/Action, and Planning axes respectively. Equip the finite label space \(L=\{0,1\}^3\) with its discrete \(\sigma\)-algebra \(2^L\). Then (i) the level sets \(C_b=\ell^{-1}(\{b\})\) for \(b\in L\) form a measurable partition of task-space into \(8\) cells; and (ii) under a fixed priority order \(P\succ T\succ M\) on loaded axes (with the empty load reserved for parcus), the assignment \(\rho:L\to\{\text{archivum},\text{cohors},\text{disciplina},\text{parcus}\}\) is total and single-valued.

Proof. (i) The family \(\{C_b\}_{b\in L}\) is the collection of preimages of singletons under \(\ell\). Distinct singletons are disjoint, so \(C_b\cap C_{b'}=\ell^{-1}(\{b\}\cap\{b'\})=\varnothing\) for \(b\neq b'\) (mutual exclusivity), and \(\bigcup_{b\in L}C_b=\ell^{-1}(L)=\) the whole space (exhaustivity), since \(\ell\) is defined on every task. Each \(\{b\}\in 2^L\), so each \(C_b\) is measurable; hence \(\{C_b\}\) is a measurable partition. As \(|L|=2^3=8\), there are exactly \(8\) cells. (ii) Define \(\rho(0,0,0)=\text{parcus}\); for \(b\neq 000\), let \(\rho(b)\) be the layer of the highest-priority loaded axis under \(P\succ T\succ M\): planning\(\to\)disciplina, else tools\(\to\)cohors, else memory\(\to\)archivum. Totality: every \(b\in L\) is either \(000\) or has a unique maximal loaded axis, so \(\rho(b)\) is defined for all \(8\) cells. Single-valuedness: the priority order is a strict total order on the three axes, so "highest-priority loaded axis" is unique, giving exactly one image; \(\rho\) is a function, not a relation. \(\square\)

In fabius. R1 computes the 3-bit load of an incoming task and lands it in exactly one of the 8 cells; the empty cell routes to parcus and any loaded cell routes to its dominant specialist under \(P\succ T\succ M\), so every task is dispatched to one and only one layer with no fall-through and no contention.

title: The capability ladder stops at the concavity knee
html:
Statement. Let the ladder be \(n\in\{0,1,\dots,N\}\). Assume value \(V\) is discrete-concave, i.e. its forward difference \(\Delta V(n):=V(n+1)-V(n)\) is non-increasing in \(n\) on \(\{0,\dots,N-1\}\); assume cost \(C\) is convex, i.e. \(\Delta C(n):=C(n+1)-C(n)\) is non-decreasing; let utility \(U:=V-C\). Define \(n^\*=\min\{n:\Delta V(n)\le\Delta C(n)\}\), with \(n^\*=N\) when that set is empty. Then \(U\) attains its maximum at \(n^\*\); the \(\le\) makes a break-even rung not worth adding.

Proof. The marginal utility is \(\Delta U(n)=U(n+1)-U(n)=\Delta V(n)-\Delta C(n)\). Since \(\Delta V\) is non-increasing and \(\Delta C\) is non-decreasing, \(-\Delta C\) is non-increasing, so \(\Delta U\) is a sum of two non-increasing sequences and is itself non-increasing: \(U\) is discrete-concave. For any \(m\), \[U(m)-U(0)=\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}\Delta U(k).\] By definition of \(n^\*\), \(\Delta U(k)=\Delta V(k)-\Delta C(k)>0\) for all \(k0\); for \(m>n^\*\), \(U(m)-U(n^\*)=\sum_{k=n^\*}^{m-1}\Delta U(k)\le 0\). Thus \(U(n^\*)\ge U(m)\) for all \(m\), so \(n^\*\) is a global maximizer. Because the defining inequality is \(\le\), a rung with \(\Delta V(n^\*)=\Delta C(n^\*)\) yields \(\Delta U(n^\*)=0\): climbing it cannot raise \(U\), so the smaller rung \(n^\*\) is selected. \(\square\)

In fabius. R2 climbs the capability ladder (inline → tool → ReAct → ToT/GoT → multi-agent) only while the marginal value of the next rung strictly exceeds its marginal cost, halting at the smallest sufficient rung \(n^\*\); the \(\le\) tie-break keeps the agent inline (or one rung lower) whenever a heavier rung merely breaks even.

title: A call must clear its expected value of information
html:
Statement. Fix a loss \(L\ge 0\) on outcomes and let an agent face two mutually exclusive actions. Inline: answer now, incurring expected loss \(a := \mathbb{E}[L\mid\text{inline}]\). Call: pay a fixed cost \(c_{\text{call}}>0\) for an observation, then act optimally on it, incurring total expected loss \(b + c_{\text{call}}\) where \(b := \mathbb{E}[L\mid\text{call}]\) is the post-observation expected loss under the call's own optimal policy. Both expectations are taken under the agent's prior; \(c_{\text{call}}\) is independent of the realized loss. Claim. The risk-minimizing action is the call iff the net value of information strictly exceeds its cost: \(a - b > c_{\text{call}}\).

Proof. The optimum is \(\min\{a,\; b + c_{\text{call}}\}\). The call is strictly preferred iff \(b + c_{\text{call}} < a\), i.e. \(a - b > c_{\text{call}}\); ties (\(=\)) and \(a-b c_{\text{call}}\), the standard cost-of-information comparison (Howard's value-of-information; Raiffa–Schlaifer). \(\;\square\)

Why \(\mathrm{EVOI}\) here is two-sided, unlike EVPI/EVSI \(\ge 0\). Both classical EVPI and classical EVSI are nonnegative, and for the same reason: the decision-maker is assumed to retain the prior-optimal (inline) action and adopt the sample's recommendation only when it improves on it. Formally, with perfect information the agent picks per realization \(\omega\) over an action set \(\mathcal{A}\) that still contains inline, so \(\min_{\alpha\in\mathcal{A}} L(\alpha,\omega)\le L(\text{inline},\omega)\); taking expectations, \(\mathbb{E}[\min_\alpha L]\le a\) and \(\mathrm{EVPI}=a-\mathbb{E}[\min_\alpha L]\ge 0\). Sample information gives \(0\le\mathrm{EVSI}\le\mathrm{EVPI}\) by the same retain-the-default argument plus the data-processing inequality. The R3 quantity \(a-b\) is not of this protected form: \(b\) is the loss under the call's own optimal policy, whose action set need not contain the inline answer and whose noisy observation may mislead. Hence \(a-b\) can be negative — a faulty tool or wrong retrieval gives \(b>a\), so \(\mathrm{EVOI}=a-b<0even at zero cost. The inequality is therefore binding in both directions: a costless-but-faulty call is rejected, and a sound-but-expensive call is rejected unless its information clears \(c_{\text{call}}\). \(\;\square\)

In fabius. R3 fires a tool/skill call only when its estimated net value \(a-b\) exceeds the call's cost \(c_{\text{call}}\) (latency + tokens + failure risk); a faulty or redundant call with \(b\ge a\) is rejected even when free, which is why this gate is two-sided rather than the trivially-nonnegative EVPI/EVSI.
issues: Attribution overstated: the block called the gate quantity a-b 'the textbook EVSI gate'. Classical EVSI (Raiffa-Schlaifer) is itself nonnegative — by the same retain-the-default argument that makes EVPI >= 0, and with EVSI <= EVPI — precisely because the decision-maker keeps the prior-optimal (inline) action and follows the sample only when it helps. That contradicts the block's own load-bearing point that a-b can be NEGATIVE. Relabeled a-b as a net value-of-information (value of the call action vs inline), distinct from textbook EVSI.

Made the EVPI/EVSI relationship explicit and correct: 0 <= EVSI <= EVPI, both nonnegative for the retain-the-default reason, whereas the R3 gate quantity is two-sided because b is computed under the call's own action set which need not contain inline. The original 'Distinction from EVPI' paragraph proved EVPI >= 0 correctly but mis-named the two-sided quantity as EVSI; the correction keeps every load-bearing step (action set still contains inline; expectation of min <= a; faulty call gives b>a so gate fails at zero cost; two-sided binding) intact.
Tie-break (=) to inline preserved; the min{a, b+c} optimum and the iff are unchanged and correct.

title: A second agent needs decorrelated error to pay
html:
Statement. Let a task be completed by one agent (the author) at expected loss \(E[L\mid\text{single}]\). Adding a second agent costs \(c_{\text{agent}}>0\) (tokens, latency, orchestration). Under the R3 marginal-value gate, spawn the second agent iff \[ E[L\mid\text{single}] - E[L\mid +\text{agent}] \;>\; c_{\text{agent}}. \] Specialize to a reviewer that only catches errors. Assume a binary outcome where the artifact contains a defect; the author fails to catch it with probability \(p_a\in(0,1)\) and an added checker independently misses it with probability \(p_c\in(0,1)\). Loss \(=1\) on an uncaught defect, \(0\) otherwise. Then under independence the joint-miss probability is \(p_a p_c\), giving strict gain \(p_a(1-p_c)\); under error-correlation \(\rho\) the gain erodes monotonically in \(\rho\). The load-bearing assumption is independence — i.e. a reviewer who did not write the artifact.

Proof. With one agent, \(E[L\mid\text{single}]=p_a\). The defect survives only if both the author and the checker miss it. Let \(A=\{\text{author misses}\}\), \(C=\{\text{checker misses}\}\), with \(\Pr(A)=p_a\), \(\Pr(C)=p_c\). Independence gives \[ E[L\mid+\text{agent}]=\Pr(A\cap C)=\Pr(A)\Pr(C)=p_a p_c. \] Hence the marginal benefit is \[ \Delta = p_a - p_a p_c = p_a(1-p_c) > 0 \quad\text{for } p_c<1, \] and \(p_a p_c < p_a\) strictly. The R3 gate fires iff \(p_a(1-p_c)>c_{\text{agent}}\). Now drop independence. By Fréchet/covariance decomposition, \[ \Pr(A\cap C)=\Pr(A)\Pr(C)+\mathrm{Cov}(\mathbf 1_A,\mathbf 1_C)=p_a p_c+\rho\sqrt{p_a(1-p_a)p_c(1-p_c)}, \] where \(\rho=\mathrm{Corr}(\mathbf 1_A,\mathbf 1_C)\). Then \[ \Delta(\rho)=p_a-\Pr(A\cap C)=p_a(1-p_c)-\rho\sqrt{p_a(1-p_a)p_c(1-p_c)}, \] so \(\partial\Delta/\partial\rho=-\sqrt{p_a(1-p_a)p_c(1-p_c)}\le 0\): the gain decreases monotonically as the two agents' errors become more correlated. At the comonotone extreme \(\rho\to+\sqrt{\tfrac{p_a(1-p_c)}{p_c(1-p_a)}}\) (with \(p_c\ge p_a\)) we get \(\Pr(A\cap C)\to p_a\) and \(\Delta\to 0\): a perfectly correlated checker — e.g. the same agent re-reading its own work — adds nothing while still costing \(c_{\text{agent}}\). \(\square\)

In fabius. cohors spawns a second agent only when the predicted defect-catch gain clears \(c_{\text{agent}}\), and it requires the reviewer to be a fresh agent that did not author the artifact — because correlated error (the author re-checking itself) drives \(\Delta\to 0\) and fails the R3 gate.

title: Plan-then-bind collapses the critical path
html:
Statement. Let an agent execute \(n\) independent tool calls, where call \(i\) incurs reasoning cost \(r_i \ge 0\) (to formulate or bind the call) and tool latency \(t_i \ge 0\) (to obtain the result). Assume the \(n\) calls are mutually independent (no call's input depends on another's output) and that tool latencies overlap freely on \(p\) executors. Bind-as-you-go interleaves reason-then-await per call, forcing a total chain \(T_{\mathrm{serial}}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}(r_i+t_i)\). Plan-then-bind first emits all reasoning against abstract placeholders, \(\sum_{i=1}^{n} r_i\), then dispatches the now-independent calls concurrently. With \(p \ge n\) executors, \(T_{\mathrm{plan}}=\sum_{i=1}^{n} r_i + \max_{i} t_i\). For \(n\) identical calls \((r_i=r,\ t_i=t)\), the speedup is \(S=T_{\mathrm{serial}}/T_{\mathrm{plan}}=\dfrac{n(r+t)}{nr+t}\), and \(S\to n\) as \(r/t \to 0\). General lower bound (Brent/Graham): \(T_{\parallel}\ge \max\!\big(\mathrm{span},\ \mathrm{work}/p\big)\).

Proof. Model the computation as a DAG: each call \(i\) is a chain \(\rho_i \to \tau_i\) of weights \(r_i\) then \(t_i\); independence means no edges cross between chains. Serial. A single executor that binds-as-you-go imposes a total order over all \(2n\) nodes, so its makespan equals their summed weight \(\sum_i (r_i+t_i)=T_{\mathrm{serial}}\). Plan. Reasoning emitted by one agent is itself serial, contributing \(\sum_i r_i\). After it completes, the \(\tau_i\) form an antichain (pairwise incomparable); with \(p\ge n\) each runs on its own executor starting simultaneously, so they finish at \(\max_i t_i\). Hence \(T_{\mathrm{plan}}=\sum_i r_i+\max_i t_i\). Speedup. For the equal case, \(S=\frac{n(r+t)}{nr+t}\); fixing \(t\) and letting \(r\to 0\), \(S\to \frac{nt}{t}=n\); equivalently \(S=n\cdot\frac{r+t}{nr+t}\uparrow n\) monotonically as \(r/t\downarrow 0\). Lower bound. The span (longest weighted path) here is \(\sum_i r_i+\max_i t_i\); no schedule beats its own critical path, giving \(T_{\parallel}\ge\mathrm{span}\). The work (total weight) is \(\sum_i r_i+\sum_i t_i\); \(p\) executors clear it no faster than \(\mathrm{work}/p\), giving \(T_{\parallel}\ge\mathrm{work}/p\). Taking the max yields the Brent/Graham bound, which \(T_{\mathrm{plan}}\) attains at \(p\ge n\). \(\square\)

In fabius. R6 routes any task with two or more mutually independent tool/sub-agent calls to plan-then-bind: emit all reasoning against placeholders first, then fan the calls out concurrently — paying \(\sum r_i+\max t_i\) instead of \(\sum(r_i+t_i)\).

Honesty boundary. The scheduling law — \(T_{\mathrm{plan}}=\sum r_i+\max_i t_i\) and \(T_{\parallel}\ge\max(\mathrm{span},\mathrm{work}/p)\) — is exact and proven here over the DAG. But the speedup magnitude \(S\to n\) was demonstrated empirically for single-tool Chain-of-Abstraction; transferring that figure to fabius's multi-agent fan-out is an analogy on the curve. title: Reason→act→observe is an invariant, not an optimum
html:
Statement. Model an agent run as a finite trace \(\tau = e_1 e_2 \cdots e_n\) of events, each a Reason, Action, or Observation. Let \(\mathrm{prov}(a)\) be the set of facts an Action \(a\) reads as preconditions, and let \(\mathrm{real}(\tau, k)\) be the facts established by Observations strictly before position \(k\). Define the grounding predicate \(G\): a trace satisfies \(G\) iff (i) for every Action \(e_k = a\), \(\mathrm{prov}(a) \subseteq \mathrm{real}(\tau,k)\) and \(\mathrm{prov}(a)\) contains no fact produced only by a Reason or by an as-yet-unobserved Action (no action is stacked on an assumed result), and (ii) progress: after any window of \(\approx 3\) consecutive cycles with no change to \(\mathrm{real}\) (no-movement), the next event is a Reason that re-plans. Claim: \(G\) is a conjoined safety + liveness invariant, and there exists no scalar objective \(J(\tau)\) that \(G\) maximizes.

Proof. This is an invariant, not an optimization: no quantity is maximized. Safety component (i) is a prefix-closed predicate — if it holds on \(\tau\) it holds on every prefix, since the gating condition at position \(k\) refers only to events before \(k\); thus violation is detected at the first ungrounded Action and "nothing bad" (acting on a fact no Observation ever returned) is excluded as a per-step guard. By the standard Alpern–Schneider decomposition, (i) is a pure safety property: its bad set is a finite-prefix property. Component (ii) is liveness: every infinite admissible continuation must eventually contain a re-plan, ruling out the unbounded stall in which the agent loops on stale assumptions — it guarantees "something good eventually happens." Their conjunction is the ReAct discipline. Now suppose, for contradiction, an objective \(J\) existed with \(G(\tau)\iff \tau\in\arg\max J\). Two grounded traces solving the same task by different tool orders both satisfy \(G\) yet are incomparable under any single \(J\) unless \(J\) is constant on the feasible set; and a constant \(J\) is maximized equally by ungrounded traces, contradicting \(G\)'s rejection of them. Hence \(G\) is definable only as a constraint on admissible traces, not as the argmax of any reward. \(\square\)

In fabius. R5 gates every tool call in disciplina/cohors on the most recent real Observation — never on a Reason-asserted or pending result — and forces a re-plan after roughly three no-movement cycles; it is enforced as an admissibility check on the control flow, never traded off against a score.

In fabius. Because it maximizes nothing, R5 is the one qualitative rule among the eighteen: the other seventeen route by comparing a quantity (cost, value, gain, EVPI), whereas R5 only ever answers admissible/inadmissible.

title: Branch only when sample information beats its cost
html:
Statement. Let \(x\) be an unknown state with prior distribution \(P(x)\), let \(a\) range over a finite action set \(A\), and let \(U(a,x)\) be a utility with \(\mathbb{E}_x[|U(a,x)|]<\infty\) for every \(a\). Define the no-information value \(V_0=\max_{a}\mathbb{E}_x[U(a,x)]\). A signal \(s\) (with any finite branching factor, i.e. any number of possible values) has joint law \(P(s,x)\); define the sample-information value \(V_1=\mathbb{E}_s\!\big[\max_a \mathbb{E}_{x\mid s}[U(a,x)]\big]\) and \(\mathrm{EVSI}=V_1-V_0\). Let \(\mathrm{EVPI}=\mathbb{E}_x[\max_a U(a,x)]-\max_a\mathbb{E}_x[U(a,x)]\). Then \(0\le\mathrm{EVSI}\le\mathrm{EVPI}\), and \(\mathrm{EVSI}=0\) whenever \(s\perp x\), for any branching factor.

Proof. Lower bound. Fix any \(a^\star\in\arg\max_a\mathbb{E}_x[U(a,x)]\). For every realized \(s\), \(\max_a\mathbb{E}_{x\mid s}[U(a,x)]\ge \mathbb{E}_{x\mid s}[U(a^\star,x)]\). Taking \(\mathbb{E}_s\) and using the tower property \(\mathbb{E}_s\mathbb{E}_{x\mid s}[U(a^\star,x)]=\mathbb{E}_x[U(a^\star,x)]=V_0\), we get \(V_1\ge V_0\), so \(\mathrm{EVSI}\ge0\). Upper bound. For each \(s\), \(\max_a\mathbb{E}_{x\mid s}[U(a,x)]\le \mathbb{E}_{x\mid s}[\max_a U(a,x)]\), since the max of expectations is at most the expectation of the pointwise max (Jensen for the convex max functional). Taking \(\mathbb{E}_s\) and applying the tower property again, \(V_1\le \mathbb{E}_x[\max_a U(a,x)]\). Subtracting \(V_0\) gives \(\mathrm{EVSI}\le\mathrm{EVPI}\). Independence. If \(s\perp x\), then \(P(x\mid s)=P(x)\), so \(\mathbb{E}_{x\mid s}[U(a,x)]=\mathbb{E}_x[U(a,x)]\) for every \(a\) and every \(s\); hence \(\max_a\mathbb{E}_{x\mid s}[U(a,x)]=V_0\) is constant in \(s\), giving \(V_1=V_0\) and \(\mathrm{EVSI}=0\) regardless of how many values \(s\) takes. \(\square\)

In fabius. R7 spawns a branch (Tree/Graph-of-Thoughts fan-out) only when an evaluator's expected information value exceeds its search cost — \(\mathrm{EVSI}>c_{\text{search}}\); since \(\mathrm{EVSI}=0\) for an evaluator uninformative about the answer (no matter how wide the branching), fabius collapses to a single ReAct chain when no cheap, discriminating evaluator exists.

title: A reducer is licensed exactly by associativity
html:
Statement. Let \(S\) be a set with a binary combiner \(\oplus:S\times S\to S\), and let inputs be finite nonempty sequences over \(S\). For a sequence \(x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\) define the serial left-fold \(F(x)=(((x_1\oplus x_2)\oplus x_3)\cdots\oplus x_n)\), and let \(R(x)\) be any order-preserving parallel reduction: the value at the root of an arbitrary binary tree whose left-to-right leaf order is \(x\), with each internal node evaluating \(\oplus\) on its children. Then \(R(x)=F(x)\) for all inputs and all trees \(\iff\) \(\oplus\) is associative, i.e. \((S,\oplus)\) is a semigroup. When \(\oplus\) is associative, \(R\) is well-defined (split-point-independent) and satisfies the concatenation law \(R(A\Vert B)=R(A)\oplus R(B)\) for all nonempty \(A,B\); thus \(R\) is a semigroup homomorphism. If additionally there exists \(e\in S\) with \(e\oplus s=s\oplus e=s\) for all \(s\), then extending the domain to admit the empty sequence with the convention \(R(\varnothing)=e\) makes \(R\) a monoid homomorphism into \((S,\oplus,e)\).

Proof. (\(\Leftarrow\)) Suppose associativity. We show every tree equals \(F\) by induction on \(n\). For \(n\le 2\) all order-preserving trees are identical, so \(R=F\). For \(n\ge 3\), any tree splits as \(\oplus(R(x_{1:k}),R(x_{k+1:n}))\) for some \(1\le k (\(\Rightarrow\)) Contrapositive: if \(\oplus\) is non-associative, pick \(a,b,c\) with \((a\oplus b)\oplus c\neq a\oplus(b\oplus c)\). The right-leaning tree on \((a,b,c)\) yields \(a\oplus(b\oplus c)\) while \(F\) yields \((a\oplus b)\oplus c\); they differ, so \(R\neq F\) on this input. Thus order-preserving-reduction\(=\)left-fold for all inputs forces associativity. \(\square\)

In fabius. M2 dispatches a single reducer/synthesis agent over parallel branches only when the combiner is associative (results genuinely merge, e.g. union, sum, max, concatenation-with-dedup); when \(\oplus\) is non-associative — branches are rival full answers that do not compose — it skips the merge and routes to best-of-\(k\), returning \(\arg\max_i v(x_i)\).

Honesty boundary. The associativity theorem above is proven about algebra and licenses the merge-vs-best-of-\(k\) decision exactly. What does NOT transfer as proof is the Graph-of-Thoughts evidence itself: Besta et al.'s aggregation gains are measured on intra-LLM thought-graph operations, a non-agent setting, so reading them as a guarantee about multi-agent branch-merging is analogy — fabius borrows the structural claim (merge needs a semigroup), not the reported numbers.
issues: Domain inconsistency: inputs are defined as 'finite nonempty' sequences, yet the original proof asserts R(∅)=e to justify the homomorphism, invoking the excluded empty sequence. Corrected by (a) stating the nonempty concatenation law R(A‖B)=R(A)⊕R(B) as a SEMIGROUP homomorphism that needs no identity e, and (b) separately upgrading to a MONOID homomorphism only by explicitly extending the domain to admit ∅ with R(∅)=e.

Overstated load-bearing role of e: the original 'homomorphism law' for nonempty A,B does not require e at all (it is just the split-at-boundary case of the ⇐ argument). The identity is load-bearing ONLY for the empty-sequence case. The correction makes this dependency explicit and notes e is two-sided so empty-side concatenation is preserved.
Clarified that R is well-defined / split-point-independent under associativity before invoking the boundary split, so the concatenation law rests on a stated fact rather than an implicit one.

title: Refine converges only under a contraction
html:
Statement. Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space and \(T:X\to X\) the refine operator, with iterate \(x_{k+1}=T(x_k)\), \(e_k=d(x_k,x^\*)\). (i) Hard oracle. If \(X\) is complete and \(T\) is a contraction, i.e. there exists \(L<1\) with \(d(T(x),T(y))\le L\,d(x,y)\) for all \(x,y\), then \(T\) has a unique fixed point \(x^\*\) and \(e_k\le L^k e_0\). (ii) Soft self-critique. If \(T\) is merely non-expansive (\(L=1\)), no convergence is guaranteed. (iii) No signal. If \(\mathbb{E}[e_{k+1}\mid e_k]=e_k\) (martingale), iteration adds expected nothing.

Proof. (i) By the triangle inequality and contraction, for \(m>k\), \(d(x_k,x_m)\le\sum_{i=k}^{m-1}d(x_i,x_{i+1})\le\sum_{i=k}^{m-1}L^i d(x_0,x_1)\le \frac{L^k}{1-L}d(x_0,x_1)\to 0\), so \((x_k)\) is Cauchy. Completeness supplies the limit \(x^\*\in X\); without it the Cauchy sequence may have no limit in \(X\) (e.g. \(T(x)=x/2+1/x\) on \(\mathbb{Q}_{>0}\) converges to \(\sqrt2\notin\mathbb{Q}\)), and no fixed point exists — completeness is necessary, not decorative. Continuity of \(T\) gives \(T(x^\*)=x^\*\); uniqueness follows since two fixed points \(x^\*,y^\*\) satisfy \(d(x^\*,y^\*)=d(T x^\*,T y^\*)\le L\,d(x^\*,y^\*)\), forcing \(d=0\). Finally \(e_{k}=d(T x_{k-1},T x^\*)\le L\,e_{k-1}\), so by induction \(e_k\le L^k e_0\), geometric decay.

(ii) With \(L=1\), the Cauchy estimate collapses (the geometric series diverges). On the unit circle a rotation \(T\) is an isometry with \(e_{k+1}=e_k\): the orbit cycles forever, never contracting. So a non-improving critic yields no contraction guarantee. (iii) If \(\mathbb{E}[e_{k+1}\mid e_k]=e_k\), then by the tower property \(\mathbb{E}[e_K]=e_0\) for every \(K\): in expectation iteration buys zero error reduction.

Cap. From \(e_k\le L^k e_0\le\mathrm{tol}\), take logs (both \(\ln L<0\) and \(\ln(\mathrm{tol}/e_0)<0\)): \(k\ge \dfrac{\ln(\mathrm{tol}/e_0)}{\ln L}\). For a moderate contraction \(L\approx 0.5\) and a one-order-of-magnitude target \(\mathrm{tol}/e_0\approx 0.1\), \(k\ge \log_2 10\approx 3.32\), so the smallest integer that meets tolerance is \(\lceil k\rceil = 4\) (indeed \(0.5^3=0.125>0.1\), while \(0.5^4=0.0625\le 0.1\)). A small hard budget of \(\approx 3\text{–}4\) passes suffices. \(\square\)

In fabius. R8 grants refine a hard \(\approx 3\text{–}4\)-iteration budget only when the loop has a hard oracle (compiler, tests, math check) that makes \(T\) a contraction; with a soft self-critique (\(L=1\)) it caps at 1–2, and on a no-signal martingale it ships after the first pass.
issues: Cap rounding error (load-bearing): the proof correctly derives k >= log_2 10 ~ 3.32 but then writes ceil(k) ~ 3. The ceiling of 3.32 is 4, and at k=3 one has e_3 = 0.5^3 e_0 = 0.125 e_0 > 0.1 e_0 = tol, so 3 iterations do NOT reach tolerance. Fixed to ceil(k) = 4, with the check 0.5^3=0.125>0.1 and 0.5^4=0.0625<=0.1 shown explicitly, and the budget restated as ~3-4.
Propagation to 'In fabius': the hard budget was stated as '~3' resting on the wrong rounding; corrected to '~3-4' so the routing claim matches the corrected arithmetic.
Minor rigor: added 'by the tower property' to justify E[e_K]=e_0 in the martingale clause (clause was correct, justification was implicit).

title: Optimal verification depth exists only because q>0
html:
Statement. Let verification effort \(v\ge 0\) on a route with measured per-route failure probability \(q\in[0,1]\) and failure cost \(C_{\mathrm{fail}}>0\). Let the detection rate \(r:[0,\infty)\to[0,1)\) be twice differentiable, strictly increasing and strictly concave (\(r'>0,\ r''<0\)), with \(r(0)=0\); note that because \(r\) is concave, increasing and bounded above by \(1\), necessarily \(r'(v)\downarrow 0\) as \(v\to\infty\). The total cost is \[ J(v)=q\,(1-r(v))\,C_{\mathrm{fail}}+\kappa v,\qquad \kappa>0. \] Then \(J\) is strictly convex; it has a unique minimizer \(v^\*\), which is interior and positive iff \(q\,C_{\mathrm{fail}}\,r'(0)>\kappa\), in which case \(v^\*=(r')^{-1}\!\big(\kappa/(qC_{\mathrm{fail}})\big)\), and otherwise \(v^\*=0\). Moreover \(\partial v^\*/\partial q>0\) on the interior regime, and \(q=0\Rightarrow v^\*=0\).

Proof. Differentiate: \(J'(v)=-q\,C_{\mathrm{fail}}\,r'(v)+\kappa\) and \(J''(v)=-q\,C_{\mathrm{fail}}\,r''(v)\). For \(q>0\), since \(C_{\mathrm{fail}}>0\) and \(r''<0\) we get \(J''>0\) everywhere, so \(J\) is strictly convex on \([0,\infty)\); hence any stationary point of the constrained problem is the unique global minimizer (KKT for a convex objective on \([0,\infty)\)). The first-order condition with the constraint \(v\ge 0\): if \(J'(0)=\kappa-q\,C_{\mathrm{fail}}\,r'(0)\ge 0\), then since \(r'\) is strictly decreasing, \(-qC_{\mathrm{fail}}r'\) is strictly increasing, so \(J'\ge0\) on \([0,\infty)\), giving the boundary solution \(v^\*=0\). If instead \(q\,C_{\mathrm{fail}}\,r'(0)>\kappa\), then \(J'(0)<0\). Now the boundedness of \(r\) is load-bearing: a concave increasing \(r\) with \(\lim_{v\to\infty}r'(v)=L>0\) would obey \(r(v)\ge r(0)+Lv\to\infty\), contradicting \(r<1\); hence \(L=0\) and \(J'(v)\to\kappa>0\). By strict monotonicity and continuity of \(J'\) there is therefore a unique interior root \[ r'(v^\*)=\frac{\kappa}{q\,C_{\mathrm{fail}}}\ \Longrightarrow\ v^\*=(r')^{-1}\!\Big(\tfrac{\kappa}{qC_{\mathrm{fail}}}\Big)>0, \] using that \(r'\) is a strictly decreasing bijection from \([0,\infty)\) onto \((0,r'(0)]\) and \(\kappa/(qC_{\mathrm{fail}})0 \] because \(r''<0\): more verification where failure is more likely. Finally, set \(q=0\): then \(J(v)=\kappa v\) is strictly increasing, minimized at \(v^\*=0\); equivalently the threshold \(q\,C_{\mathrm{fail}}\,r'(0)>\kappa\) fails for \(q=0\) since the left side is \(0<\kappa\). The optimal depth is positive only because \(q>0\). \(\square\)

q estimation. \(q\) is not known a priori; maintain a Beta–Bernoulli posterior per route. With prior \(q\sim\mathrm{Beta}(\alpha_0,\beta_0)\) and \(s\) observed failures in \(n\) i.i.d. executions, conjugacy gives the posterior \(\mathrm{Beta}(\alpha_0+s,\ \beta_0+n-s)\), and the plug-in posterior-mean estimate \(\hat q=(\alpha_0+s)/(\alpha_0+\beta_0+n)\) feeds the threshold and \(v^\*\) online; as \(n\) grows the posterior concentrates and \(v^\*\) tracks the true rate. (Plugging \(\hat q\) into the nonlinear threshold is a point approximation, not the full posterior-averaged Bayes decision.)

In fabius. M3 sets the corrector/verification depth on each route: spend nonzero verification effort exactly when \(\hat q\,C_{\mathrm{fail}}\,r'(0)>\kappa\) (deeper where the Beta–Bernoulli \(\hat q\) is higher), and attach no corrector to routes that never fail (\(\hat q\approx 0\Rightarrow v^\*=0\)) — YAGNI as a theorem.
issues: Limit step under-justified: proof claims J'(v)→κ from 'r'(v)→L≥0' but that only gives J'(v)→κ−qC_fail·L; the needed L=0 is not implied by r''<0 alone. Fixed by invoking boundedness of r (concave + increasing + r<1 ⟹ r'→0), now stated as a load-bearing assumption/step.
Malformed expression 'r'(v)→L≥0≤r'(0)' removed and replaced with a correct argument.
Made explicit that r' is a bijection onto (0, r'(0)] and that the threshold value κ/(qC_fail) lies in that range, so the interior root exists and is finite (ruling out v*=+∞).
Added 'i.i.d.' to the Beta–Bernoulli observations and noted the plug-in posterior-mean is a point approximation, not the full posterior-averaged Bayes decision.

title: Reflect-then-retry is optimal stopping
html:
Statement. Fix a failed attempt and let \(V_{\text{fix}}>0\) be the value of eventually succeeding, \(c_{\text{retry}}>0\) the cost of one more reflect-and-retry round, and \(p_{k+1}\in[0,1]\) the probability that attempt \(k+1\) succeeds given the history \(R_{myopic one-step lookahead: at each step the agent compares stopping now against taking exactly one more attempt and then stopping. Then the marginal value of attempt \(k+1\) is \(\Delta V_{k+1}=p_{k+1}\,V_{\text{fix}}-c_{\text{retry}}\), and the optimal myopic policy is to continue while \(p_{k+1}>c_{\text{retry}}/V_{\text{fix}}\) and stop otherwise.

Proof. Under one-step lookahead the value of stopping is \(0\) (no further reward, no further cost). The value of one more round is the expected gain net of its cost, \(\mathbb{E}[\text{gain}]-c_{\text{retry}} = p_{k+1}V_{\text{fix}} + (1-p_{k+1})\cdot 0 - c_{\text{retry}} = \Delta V_{k+1}\). A rational agent continues iff continuing dominates stopping, i.e. \(\Delta V_{k+1}>0 \iff p_{k+1}V_{\text{fix}}>c_{\text{retry}} \iff p_{k+1}>c_{\text{retry}}/V_{\text{fix}}\), which is exactly the stated threshold rule.

title: Accept a rewrite only on a held-out risk drop
html:
Statement. Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be a finite class of candidate prompts. Each prompt \(p\) has a true risk \(R(p)=\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}}[\ell(p,x)]\) with bounded loss \(\ell(p,x)\in[0,1]\). Let \(D_{\mathrm{val}}=\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}\) be drawn i.i.d. from \(\mathcal{D}\), independent of how \(\mathcal{P}\) was assembled, and let \(\widehat{R}(p)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \ell(p,x_i)\). Let \(\hat p\in\arg\min_{p\in\mathcal{P}}\widehat{R}(p)\) (ERM). Then with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[ R(\hat p)\;\le\;\min_{p\in\mathcal{P}}R(p)\;+\;2\sqrt{\frac{\ln|\mathcal{P}|+\ln(2/\delta)}{2n}}. \]

Proof. Fix \(p\). The terms \(\ell(p,x_i)\) are i.i.d. in \([0,1]\) with mean \(R(p)\). Hoeffding's inequality gives, for any \(t>0\), \(\Pr[|\widehat{R}(p)-R(p)|>t]\le 2e^{-2nt^2}\). Set \(t=\varepsilon:=\sqrt{(\ln|\mathcal{P}|+\ln(2/\delta))/(2n)}\), so \(2e^{-2n\varepsilon^2}=\delta/|\mathcal{P}|\). Union-bounding over the \(|\mathcal{P}|\) prompts, \[ \Pr\!\Big[\exists\, p\in\mathcal{P}:|\widehat{R}(p)-R(p)|>\varepsilon\Big]\le|\mathcal{P}|\cdot\frac{\delta}{|\mathcal{P}|}=\delta. \] So on an event \(E\) of probability \(\ge 1-\delta\), \(|\widehat{R}(p)-R(p)|\le\varepsilon\) holds simultaneously for every \(p\). Let \(p^\star\in\arg\min_{p}R(p)\). On \(E\): \[ R(\hat p)\;\le\;\widehat{R}(\hat p)+\varepsilon\;\le\;\widehat{R}(p^\star)+\varepsilon\;\le\;R(p^\star)+2\varepsilon, \] where the first and third steps use uniform concentration and the middle step uses that \(\hat p\) minimizes \(\widehat{R}\) (hence \(\widehat{R}(\hat p)\le\widehat{R}(p^\star)\)). Substituting \(\varepsilon\) yields the claim. \(\square\)

In fabius. M5 accepts a rewrite \(p'\) over \(p\) only when \(\widehat{R}(p')<\widehat{R}(p)\) on the held-out \(D_{\mathrm{val}}\); the bound certifies that an empirical drop transfers to true risk up to \(2\varepsilon\), so a rewrite that merely "sounds better" but shows no measured \(\widehat{R}\) delta is rejected, and the gate tightens as \(n\) grows.

title: A verified skill is a memoized sub-solution
html:
Statement. Let a task decompose into subproblems whose dependency relation forms a DAG with \(n\) distinct nodes, and assume (i) optimal substructure — an optimal solution is composed of optimal solutions to its subproblems — and (ii) overlapping subproblems — the naive recursion revisits the same nodes exponentially often. Model a verified, retrieval-keyed skill as a memo table \(M[s]\): on a hit, return the stored solution in \(O(1)\) plus a verify-predicate \(V(s)\); on a miss, compute and store. Then memoized evaluation performs \(\Theta(2^n)\) → \(O(n)\) work (each subproblem solved once), and the expected per-call cost is \((1-h)\,c_{\text{compute}} + h\,c_{\text{lookup}}\) with hit rate \(h\) and \(c_{\text{lookup}} \ll c_{\text{compute}}\).

Proof. Naive recomputation of a recurrence whose call tree branches (e.g. \(T(n)=2T(n-1)+\Theta(1)\)) satisfies \(T(n)=\Theta(2^n)\): the tree has exponentially many leaves because each overlapping subproblem is re-expanded independently. Now equip the recursion with \(M\). Charge each invocation to one of two buckets. A node \(s\) is first-seen at most once: at that point \(M[s]\) is empty, we pay \(c_{\text{compute}}(s)\) and write the result; by optimal substructure this stored value is a correct optimal sub-solution, so it never needs recomputation. Every later invocation on \(s\) hits \(M\) and pays only \(c_{\text{lookup}}+V(s)=O(1)\). First-seen work therefore sums over the \(n\) distinct nodes once: \(\sum_{s} c_{\text{compute}}(s) = O(n)\) for \(O(1)\) per-node cost (more generally \(O(n)\) calls each doing bounded local work over its in-edges, \(O(n+E)\)). Hit work is absorbed into the \(O(1)\) charge of the calling edge. Summing the disjoint buckets gives \(O(n)\), collapsing the exponential. Amortized over a call stream with hit rate \(h\), expected cost \(=(1-h)\,c_{\text{compute}}+h\,c_{\text{lookup}}\); since \(c_{\text{lookup}}\ll c_{\text{compute}}\), this is monotone decreasing in \(h\) and tends to \(c_{\text{lookup}}\). \(\square\)

In fabius. M6 forces retrieve-before-plan: before spending a compute step, query the skill/memory store keyed by the subproblem; a verified hit is returned at lookup cost and a miss is computed once and written back — so identical sub-solutions are reused, never re-derived, and "supersede-don't-duplicate" keeps each key solved a single time.

title: Eviction is lossless because addresses are a code
html:
Statement. Fix a fast tier of capacity \(B\) (bytes of window occupancy) and an unbounded slow tier. An eviction write=EVICT moves a fact \(f\) of length \(\ell(f)\) to an addressed page and leaves in the window a pointer [[slug]] of length \(\ell(\text{slug})\). Assume (i) addresses are drawn from a fixed alphabet of size \(D\); (ii) the addressing scheme is uniquely decodable — distinct stored facts always receive distinct, unambiguously parseable slugs, so the address-to-page map is injective and total; and (iii) eviction is byte-gated: M7 evicts \(f\) only when \(\ell(\text{slug})\le\ell(f)\) (the pointer is no longer than the fact it replaces). Let the multiset of address lengths in use be \(\{\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n\}\). Then a slug code with these lengths can coexist (the Kraft sum is satisfiable), eviction is byte-exact reversible, and each eviction leaves total stored information non-decreasing while never increasing window occupancy (it drops it by \(\ell(f)-\ell(\text{slug})\ge 0\)).

Proof. Necessity (McMillan). For any uniquely-decodable code, consider the \(k\)-fold extension. The generating identity \(\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} D^{-\ell_i}\right)^{k}=\sum_{m=k\ell_{\min}}^{k\ell_{\max}} A_m\,D^{-m}\), where \(A_m\) counts length-\(k\) source strings whose concatenated codewords have total length \(m\). Unique decodability forces injectivity onto \(D\)-ary strings of length \(m\), so \(A_m\le D^{m}\), giving each term \(A_m D^{-m}\le 1\); the sum has at most \(k\ell_{\max}-k\ell_{\min}+1\le k\,\ell_{\max}\) terms (as \(\ell_{\min}\ge 1\)), so \(\left(\sum_i D^{-\ell_i}\right)^{k}\le k\,\ell_{\max}\). Taking \(k\)-th roots and \(k\to\infty\), the right side \((k\ell_{\max})^{1/k}\to 1\), yielding \(\sum_i D^{-\ell_i}\le 1\). Sufficiency (Kraft). Conversely, if \(\sum_i D^{-\ell_i}\le 1\), sort lengths and assign codewords greedily on the \(D\)-ary tree; the inequality guarantees enough unused subtrees, producing a prefix (hence uniquely-decodable) code. Thus such a code exists iff \(\sum_i D^{-\ell_i}\le 1\). By assumption (ii) the slug scheme IS uniquely decodable, so its lengths satisfy the inequality, and decoding recovers each slug exactly; following the address fetches \(f\) byte-for-byte. Hence eviction is a bijection between \((f \text{ in window})\) and \((\text{slug in window}, f \text{ on page})\): no information is destroyed, only relocated, so stored information is non-decreasing. By assumption (iii), occupancy changes by \(-(\ell(f)-\ell(\text{slug}))\le 0\), so each eviction is byte-exact reversible and non-increasing in window occupancy. \(\square\)

In fabius. M7 routes a fact to write=EVICT when the window would exceed \(B\), but only when \(\ell(\text{slug})\le\ell(f)\): flush \(f\) to an addressed page, keep only [[slug]], and trust that the unique decodability of the address guarantees byte-exact recall — so the eviction frees \(\ell(f)-\ell(\text{slug})\ge 0\) of budget with zero loss, monotonically drawing occupancy back toward \(\le B\).
issues: Occupancy overstatement: the original wrote the savings \(\ell(f)-\ell(\text{slug})\ge 0\) as if self-evident, but nothing in assumptions (i)-(ii) forces a slug to be no longer than the fact it replaces. A short fact with a long slug would INCREASE occupancy, breaking both the '\(\ge 0\)' claim and 'occupancy stays \(\le B\)'. This non-negativity is a load-bearing hypothesis, not a consequence of unique decodability. Fixed by adding explicit byte-gating assumption (iii): M7 evicts only when \(\ell(\text{slug})\le\ell(f)\).

'window occupancy stays \(\le B\)' is too strong as a per-eviction guarantee: eviction is triggered precisely because occupancy would exceed \(B\), and a single eviction need not restore \(\le B\). The defensible claim is that each (gated) eviction is non-increasing in occupancy, monotonically driving it back toward \(\le B\). Restated accordingly in both the Statement and the 'In fabius' note.

Minor exposition tightening in the McMillan step: made explicit that each term \(A_m D^{-m}\le 1\) and that the number of terms is \(\le k\ell_{\max}\) (using \(\ell_{\min}\ge 1\)), and that \((k\ell_{\max})^{1/k}\to 1\). The original's 'the right side's exponent vanishes' was correct but terse; no mathematical error there.

title: Retrieval under a budget is submodular knapsack
html:
Statement. Let \(P\) be a set of candidate pages, each with token length \(\mathrm{len}(p)>0\), and a budget \(B\). Let \(f:2^{P}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\) be the relevance of a retrieved set, assumed monotone (\(A\subseteq B\Rightarrow f(A)\le f(B)\)) and submodular: for all \(A\subseteq B\) and \(p\notin B\), \(f(A\cup\{p\})-f(A)\ge f(B\cup\{p\})-f(B)\). Submodularity is the realistic model: two pages covering the same fact have overlapping relevance, so each added page's marginal usefulness diminishes. We maximize \(f(S)\) subject to \(\sum_{p\in S}\mathrm{len}(p)\le B\). (i) Plain marginal-gain greedy (pick the feasible page of largest absolute gain, ignoring cost) has unbounded approximation ratio. (ii) Cost-benefit greedy with partial enumeration of seed sets of size \(\le 3\) achieves \(1-1/e\) (Sviridenko; Khuller–Moss–Naor — their plain modified greedy alone gives only \(1-1/\sqrt{e}\), enumeration recovers \(1-1/e\)).

Proof. (i) Fix an integer \(B\ge 2\) and a parameter \(M>2\). Construct one expensive page \(p_0\) with \(\mathrm{len}(p_0)=B\) and singleton value \(M\), and \(B\) cheap pages \(q_1,\dots,q_B\), each \(\mathrm{len}(q_i)=1\), with \(f\) additive over \(\{q_i\}\) and per-page gain \(M/B + 1\) (additive functions are submodular). Plain marginal-gain greedy compares absolute gains while feasible: the first move sees \(p_0\) with gain \(M\) versus each \(q_i\) with gain \(M/B+12\), greedy takes \(r\) and matches OPT, so cost-ignoring greedy's failure needs budget blocking, not value blocking. The canonical unbounded instance: pages \(a\) (\(\mathrm{len}=1,\ \text{gain}=1+\varepsilon\)) and \(b\) (\(\mathrm{len}=B,\ \text{gain}=M\)), additive, with the modification that after greedy commits to the locally-largest *unit-feasible* gain it is forced to spend on \(a\)-type fillers. Concretely give greedy \(B\) filler pages each \(\mathrm{len}=1,\ \text{gain}=1+\varepsilon\), so it consumes the whole budget on fillers for total \((1+\varepsilon)B\), while OPT takes the single page \(b\) of cost \(B\) and value \(M\). Choosing \(M\gg(1+\varepsilon)B\) yields ratio \((1+\varepsilon)B/M\to0\). Plain greedy is arbitrarily bad. (ii) For each seed \(S_0\) with \(|S_0|\le 3\), run cost-benefit greedy (add the feasible \(p\) maximizing the density \(\bigl(f(S\cup\{p\})-f(S)\bigr)/\mathrm{len}(p)\)) on \(P\setminus S_0\); return the best result over all seeds. Monotone submodularity gives, at every greedy state \(S\), the covering inequality \(f(\mathrm{OPT})-f(S)\le\sum_{p\in\mathrm{OPT}\setminus S}\bigl(f(S\cup\{p\})-f(S)\bigr)\); dividing each term by \(\mathrm{len}(p)\) and re-weighting by \(\mathrm{len}(p)\) shows the densest feasible pick captures at least a \(\mathrm{len}(p)/B\) fraction of the residual gap, which drives the standard \(1-1/e\) recursion. Enumerating the (at most) three highest-value elements of \(\mathrm{OPT}\) as a seed removes the boundary item that a density-only argument can drop on the last partial step. Hence the returned \(S\) satisfies \(f(S)\ge(1-1/e)\,f(\mathrm{OPT})\). \(\square\)

In fabius. R9 governs how archivum fills a retrieval token budget: never rank pages by raw relevance, rank by relevance-per-token (cost-benefit) with a small seed sweep, so one long page can't crowd out several denser ones — exactly the knapsack failure plain top-\(k\) commits.
issues: Part (i) as written is non-rigorous and internally contradictory: it openly thrashes ('No — it takes...', 'instead let...', 'with the twist that...') and conflates two distinct failure mechanisms (largest-absolute-gain vs budget-exhaustion). The numeric setup f({p1})=2, f({p2})=M with M>2 actually makes cost-ignoring greedy pick the GOOD item p2 and match OPT, so it does not establish unboundedness — the stated example proves the opposite of the claim. The claim itself (plain greedy unbounded) is true, but the proof must reach it via a valid instance.

The expression in (ii), \(\sum_{p}\frac{f(S\cup\{p\})-f(S)}{\mathrm{len}(p)}\mathrm{len}(p)\), trivially cancels to \(\sum_p (f(S\cup\{p\})-f(S))\); writing the density and its inverse weight in the same term is a dimensional slip. Corrected to state the submodular covering inequality first, then divide/re-weight to justify the density rule.

Attribution was thin: the bound credited 'Khuller–Moss–Naor; Sviridenko' without noting that KMN's plain modified greedy gives only \(1-1/\sqrt{e}\) and that partial enumeration (the load-bearing ingredient the Statement names) is exactly what lifts it to \(1-1/e\). Made explicit so the (1-1/e) bound is not silently attributed to greedy alone.

title: Index-first prefiltering is a mutual-information cut
html:
Statement. Let the target \(X\) be drawn over a finite universe \(U\), and let a cheap symbolic index emit a value \(Y\) that deterministically restricts the candidate set to \(C(Y)=\{x: \text{test passes}\}\subseteq U\). Assuming \(X\) is uniform on \(U\) and uniform on \(C(Y)\) given \(Y\), the search entropy falls from \(H(X)=\log_2|U|\) to \(H(X\mid Y)=\mathbb{E}_Y[\log_2|C(Y)|]\), and the expected reduction is the mutual information \(I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X\mid Y)\ge 0\). Under per-comparison costs \(c_{\text{index}},c_{\text{rerank}}\), the two-stage cascade \(c_{\text{index}}|U|+c_{\text{rerank}}|C|\) beats single-stage \(c_{\text{rerank}}|U|\) iff \(c_{\text{index}}/c_{\text{rerank}}<1-|C|/|U|\); and if the test is relevance-monotone (it never excludes a truly relevant item), recall@\(C\approx 1\).

Proof. Identifying entropy with the bits needed to locate \(X\): uniformity gives \(H(X)=\log_2|U|\). Conditioning on \(Y\), \(X\) is uniform on \(C(Y)\), so \(H(X\mid Y=y)=\log_2|C(y)|\) and \(H(X\mid Y)=\mathbb{E}_Y[\log_2|C(Y)|]\). By definition \(I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X\mid Y)\), and by Jensen (concavity of \(\log\)) or the non-negativity of KL divergence, \(I(X;Y)\ge 0\), with equality iff \(X\perp Y\) — i.e. a useless index. Thus the index removes exactly \(I(X;Y)\) bits of search.

For cost: \(c_{\text{index}}|U|+c_{\text{rerank}}|C|

In fabius. R9b governs archivum retrieval: run the cheap symbolic index/tag/keyword filter first to cut \(U\) to \(C\), then spend the expensive dense rerank only on \(C\) — provably cheaper whenever the symbolic test is near-free and selective, and lossless in recall when it is relevance-monotone.

title: Summarize-then-link is rate–distortion with lossless recovery
html:
Statement. Let \(S\) be the source page (a random variable over a finite alphabet \(\mathcal{S}\)) and let \(\hat{S}\) be an inlined summary drawn through a channel \(p(\hat{s}\mid s)\). Fix a distortion measure \(d:\mathcal{S}\times\hat{\mathcal{S}}\to[0,\infty)\) with the recoverability property \(d(s,\hat s)=0\iff s=\hat s\) (so \(\hat{\mathcal{S}}\supseteq\mathcal{S}\)). The Shannon rate–distortion function is \[ R(D)=\min_{\,p(\hat{s}\mid s)\,:\,\mathbb{E}[d(S,\hat{S})]\le D}\; I(S;\hat{S}). \] Assume (i) \(\mathcal{S}\) is nondegenerate, so \(H(S)>0\); (ii) the inlined view has a hard rate budget \(B0\), where \(D(B)=\inf\{D:R(D)\le B\}\); yet the stored page reached through the link \([[\texttt{slug}]]\) carries distortion \(0\).

Proof. Under the recoverability property, \(R(D)\) is convex, nonincreasing and continuous on \([0,D_{\max}]\), with \(R(D)=0\) for \(D\ge D_{\max}=\min_{\hat{s}}\mathbb{E}[d(S,\hat s)]\) and \(R(0)=I(S;S)=H(S)\) (discrete, finite-alphabet case). An inlined view with \(I(S;\hat S)\le B\) is constrained accordingly. By the converse to the rate–distortion theorem, no test channel with \(I(S;\hat S)\le B\) can achieve expected distortion below \(D(B)\). Since \(B0\). Thus operating at rate \(B\) forces accepted distortion \(D(B)>0\) on what is paged into context. Now consider storage. The summary is emitted with a pointer \([[\texttt{slug}]]\) resolving to the verbatim page. The composite stored object is \((\hat S,\texttt{slug})\); the recovery map \(g(\texttt{slug})=S\) is deterministic and exact, so the second coordinate alone reconstructs the source: \(d(S,g(\texttt{slug}))=0\) almost surely, i.e. the stored record realizes the point \((D{=}0,R{=}H(S))\) on the curve. The loss \(D(B)\) is confined to the inlined projection \(\hat S\); it is not a property of the stored record. Finally, the information bottleneck replaces the distortion constraint with the Lagrangian \(\min\, I(S;\hat S)-\beta\,I(\hat S;Y)\), measuring fidelity as relevance \(I(\hat S;Y)\) retained about a target \(Y\); rate–distortion is the special case in which the relevance term reduces to reconstruction error of \(S\) itself. So summarize-then-link is the \(\beta\)-weighted bottleneck with \(Y=\) the query the page must still answer: the inline view trades rate for relevance, the linked page restores full \(I(S;Y)\). \(\square\)

In fabius. When a write would exceed the context/token budget \(B\), archivum does not truncate destructively: it inlines a budget-fitted summary (accepting \(D(B)\)) and emits a \([[\texttt{slug}]]\) to the full page, so the paged-in view is lossy but the stored record is recoverable at zero distortion.
issues: Recoverability property d(s,s_hat)=0 iff s=s_hat was used to assert R(0)=H(S) but only stated parenthetically mid-proof; promoted it into the Statement's hypotheses where it is load-bearing, and noted hat-S alphabet must contain S for zero distortion to be achievable.

Source alphabet should be finite/discrete for R(0)=H(S) and continuity to hold cleanly; the original said 'random variable over messages' loosely. Pinned to finite alphabet so the converse, convexity, continuity and R(0)=H(S) are all valid (in general/continuous sources R(0) need not equal H(S)).

The budget B is a per-symbol RATE (bits per source symbol), the natural argument of R; original wavered between 'tokens'/'bits'. Stated B as a rate budget so 'I(S;hat S)<=B' is dimensionally the right constraint feeding R(D); the 'In fabius' application keeps the informal token reading, which is fine operationally.

Strict monotonicity claim: R is strictly decreasing only on the region where R>0 (it is flat at 0 for D>=D_max). Original wrote 'strictly decreasing on [0,D_max]'. Corrected to 'strictly decreasing where it is positive' so the inversion D(B) is justified exactly on the relevant range, which is where B<R(0) places it.

No overstatement of the analogy: the information-bottleneck paragraph correctly frames RD as a special case and does not claim it proves anything beyond the transmitted/stored decomposition; left intact with tightened wording.

title: Rank by probability of relevance (PRP)
html:
Statement. Fix a query \(q\) and a finite set of index pages \(\{p_1,\dots,p_n\}\). For each page let \(\pi_i := P(\text{relevant}\mid q, p_i)\), and assume (i) relevance judgements are made independently per page given \(q\) (so the relevance indicators \(R_i\in\{0,1\}\) have \(\mathbb{E}[R_i]=\pi_i\) and the value of a page does not depend on which other pages are surfaced), and (ii) uniform retrieval cost — every page costs the same to inspect, so a ranking is just a permutation and the only choice is order. Let a ranking present pages in order \(\sigma(1),\dots,\sigma(n)\). Then ranking by descending \(\pi_i\) maximizes the expected number of relevant pages among the top \(k\), for every cutoff \(k\) simultaneously; hence it maximizes expected precision \(P@k\) and expected recall \(R@k\) at every \(k\), and is Bayes-optimal.

Proof. The expected count of relevant pages in the top \(k\) is, by linearity of expectation (no independence needed for this step), \(\mathbb{E}[\#\text{rel}@k]=\sum_{j=1}^{k}\pi_{\sigma(j)}\). For a fixed budget \(k\), \(\sum_{j=1}^{k}\pi_{\sigma(j)}\) is the sum of \(k\) elements drawn from \(\{\pi_i\}\); a sum of \(k\) reals is maximized by choosing the \(k\) largest, i.e. by placing the top-\(\pi\) pages first. The descending-\(\pi\) permutation \(\sigma^\star\) puts the \(k\) largest \(\pi\) in positions \(1..k\) for every \(k\) at once (a prefix of a sorted list is its own top-\(k\)), so it is simultaneously optimal at all cutoffs. Then \(\mathbb{E}[P@k]=\tfrac1k\sum_{j\le k}\pi_{\sigma(j)}\) and \(\mathbb{E}[R@k]=\tfrac1{\,\mathbb{E}[\#\text{rel}]\,}\sum_{j\le k}\pi_{\sigma(j)}\), where \(\mathbb{E}[\#\text{rel}]=\sum_i\pi_i\) is constant in \(\sigma\); each is a monotone-increasing function of the same maximized prefix sum, so both are maximized by \(\sigma^\star\). What licenses "pick the \(k\) largest" is the additive form of the objective, which comes from linearity of expectation alone. The role of independence is upstream of that: it guarantees each page's contribution is its own \(\pi_i\) with no inter-document coupling — no page's relevance value is altered by, or redundant with, the others already surfaced — so the per-page scores \(\pi_i\) are exactly the marginal contributions being summed. (When relevance is correlated — e.g. near-duplicate or novelty effects — this marginal-equals-total identification fails and greedy-by-\(\pi\) can be beaten, the classical limit of PRP.) Uniform cost guarantees the feasible set is all permutations (no item is cheaper to surface), so no cost-adjusted reordering can beat the sort. This is the Robertson (1977) PRP; optimality of the posterior-mean ordering is Bayes-optimality. Utility generalization. Let load-bearingness \(u(p_i)\ge0\) weight each page. Expected utility of the top \(k\) is \(\sum_{j\le k} u(p_{\sigma(j)})\,\pi_{\sigma(j)}\); the identical exchange/sorting argument on the scores \(s_i:=u(p_i)\,\pi_i\) shows descending-\(s\) is optimal at every cutoff. \(\square\)

In fabius. M8 ranks archivum index entries by \(P(\text{relevant}\mid q,\text{page})\) and retrieves the top few; when pages differ in load-bearingness it ranks by \(s=u(\text{page})\cdot P(\text{relevant}\mid q,\text{page})\), with \(u\) entering strictly as an outer utility weight — never folded into the bare relevance probability that PRP optimizes.
issues: Incorrect attribution: the proof claimed independence 'licenses pick the k largest' by making the objective decompose additively. The additive decomposition follows from linearity of expectation alone (the proof even says 'no independence needed yet'), not from independence. Fixed by attributing additivity to linearity and reassigning independence to its true role: identifying each pi as the page's marginal, non-redundant contribution (the assumption whose failure under correlated/duplicate relevance is the known PRP breakdown).

Assumption (i) originally stated only E[R_i]=pi_i, which is a marginal condition that does not by itself capture the no-inter-document-coupling content that PRP actually needs; strengthened the wording of (i) to state that a page's value does not depend on which other pages are surfaced.
Minor: made explicit that the recall normalizer E[#rel]=sum_i pi_i is constant in sigma, which is what makes maximizing the prefix sum maximize expected recall.

title: Synthesize logs when MDL says so
html:
Statement. Let \(L=(l_1,\dots,l_n)\) be a batch of log lines drawn from a countable line-alphabet \(\mathcal{A}\). Fix a prefix-free coding scheme, write \(\ell(\cdot)\) for codeword length in bits, and let \(L(\cdot)=\ell(\cdot)\) denote description length. A synthesis page is a model \(p\) (a hypothesis/dictionary) under which the batch is re-encoded, giving a two-part code of length \(L(p)+L(L\mid p)\), where \(L(L\mid p)\) is the length of \(L\) encoded relative to \(p\). The raw code stores each line independently at cost \(\sum_{i=1}^n L(l_i)\). Assume both codes are uniquely decodable (each is a valid prefix code, so each satisfies Kraft: \(\sum 2^{-\ell}\le 1\)). Claim. Under the Minimum Description Length principle one should adopt the synthesis page exactly when

\[ L(p) + L(L \mid p) \;<\; \sum_{i=1}^{n} L(l_i). \]

Proof. MDL selects, among admissible descriptions of the data, the one of minimum total length — the operational reading of "the best hypothesis compresses best," itself a computable proxy for Kolmogorov complexity \(K\), which is uncomputable but satisfies \(K(x)\le \ell(x)+O(1)\) for every computable prefix code and so lower-bounds each. Both candidates are admissible descriptions of the same object \(L\): by unique decodability each lets a receiver reconstruct \(l_1,\dots,l_n\) exactly, so comparing their lengths is comparing two lossless encodings of one message. MDL's decision rule is therefore the total order on lengths: prefer \(p\) iff \(L(p)+L(L\mid p) < \sum_i L(l_i)\), which is the claim. The content of the inequality is structural. The raw cost \(\sum_i L(l_i)\) pays full price per line. The two-part cost splits into model cost \(L(p)\) — paid once — and residual \(L(L\mid p)=\sum_i L(l_i\mid p)\), the lines re-encoded against the shared regularities \(p\) captures. Define the redundancy \(R=\sum_i\big(L(l_i)-L(l_i\mid p)\big)\), the net bits saved across lines by encoding through \(p\). The criterion then rearranges by pure algebra to \(L(p) < R\): synthesis wins precisely when the inter-line redundancy strictly exceeds the summary's own description cost. Note \(R\) need not be nonnegative — for a poorly fitted or mis-specified \(p\) a conditional codeword may be longer than the unconditional one on these particular realized lines, since pointwise codeword length is not bounded by entropy (the inequality \(H(l_i\mid p)\le H(l_i)\) governs only expected optimal length, not the length of a fixed outcome). When \(R\le 0\) the residual already matches or exceeds the raw cost and MDL keeps the lines regardless of \(L(p)\); when \(R>0\) but \(R\le L(p)\) the savings fail to amortize the summary, and again raw wins. Synthesis is justified exactly at \(R>L(p)\), and not before. \(\square\)

In fabius. archivum folds a grown batch of log lines into a synthesis page only when the page's description cost \(L(p)\) is strictly paid back by net cross-line redundancy \(R=\sum_i(L(l_i)-L(l_i\mid p))>L(p)\); until the log accumulates enough genuinely shared structure to make that two-part code shorter, the raw lines stay, so synthesis fires precisely at the MDL break-even and never on a still-incompressible log.
issues: Entropy-to-pointwise confusion: the proof claimed 'By Shannon's source-coding bound the achievable residual per line is governed by H(l_i|p) <= H(l_i)... exploiting redundancy can only shorten, never lengthen, the optimal per-line code.' The entropy inequality H(l_i|p) <= H(l_i) is about EXPECTED optimal code length, not the realized codeword length L(l_i|p) of a specific fixed line. For an individual outcome (and for a mis-specified p) a conditional code can be strictly longer. The argument does not establish a per-line shortening.

Unsupported sign claim R >= 0: the proof asserted the redundancy R = sum(L(l_i) - L(l_i|p)) >= 0 and derived it from the (inapplicable) entropy inequality. R is not guaranteed nonnegative for realized lengths or a bad p. This is over-asserted and not load-bearing — MDL requires L(p) < R, not R >= 0. Corrected to note R may be negative and that raw wins whenever R <= L(p) (covering both R<=0 and 0<R<=L(p)).

Tightened the Kolmogorov-complexity remark to the precise statement K(x) <= l(x) + O(1) (K lower-bounds each computable prefix code up to a constant), replacing the loose 'lower-bounds every prefix code'.

Preserved the correct results: the MDL decision rule L(p)+L(L|p) < sum L(l_i) and its algebraic rearrangement to L(p) < R are exact and retained; the 'In fabius' mapping was made consistent with the two-sided R (synthesis iff R > L(p)).

title: Flow matching: marginal = average of conditionals (analogy)
html:
Statement. Fix a data coupling \(z\sim q\) and, for each \(z\), a conditional probability path \(t\mapsto p_t(\cdot\mid z)\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\) generated by a conditional velocity field \(u_t(\cdot\mid z)\), meaning each conditional satisfies the continuity equation \(\partial_t p_t(x\mid z)+ abla\!\cdot\! ig(p_t(x\mid z)\,u_t(x\mid z) ig)=0\). Define the marginal \(p_t(x)=\int p_t(x\mid z)\,q(z)\,dz\). Assume \(p_t(x)>0\) on the support and enough regularity to differentiate under the integral. Then the marginal field defined as the posterior average \[ u_t(x)\;=\;\mathbb{E} ig[u_t(x\mid z)\mid x_t=x ig]\;=\;\int u_t(x\mid z)\, rac{p_t(x\mid z)\,q(z)}{p_t(x)}\,dz \] generates \(p_t\): \(\partial_t p_t+ abla\!\cdot\!(p_t u_t)=0\). Flow-matching learns \(u_t\) by regressing a network onto the (cheap) conditional targets \(u_t(x\mid z)\).

Proof. Define the marginal flux \(J_t(x)=\int u_t(x\mid z)\,p_t(x\mid z)\,q(z)\,dz\). Dividing and multiplying by \(p_t(x)\) gives \(J_t(x)=p_t(x)\int u_t(x\mid z)\, frac{p_t(x\mid z)q(z)}{p_t(x)}\,dz=p_t(x)\,u_t(x)\), which is exactly the posterior-average identity. Now differentiate the marginal in time and exchange order: \[ \partial_t p_t(x)=\int \partial_t p_t(x\mid z)\,q(z)\,dz=-\int abla\!\cdot\! ig(u_t(x\mid z)p_t(x\mid z) ig)q(z)\,dz, \] using the conditional continuity equation. Since \(q(z)\) is \(x\)-independent, pull \( abla\cdot\) outside the \(z\)-integral: \[ \partial_t p_t(x)=- abla\!\cdot\!\!\int u_t(x\mid z)p_t(x\mid z)q(z)\,dz=- abla\!\cdot\!J_t(x)=- abla\!\cdot\! ig(p_t(x)u_t(x) ig). \] Hence \(\partial_t p_t+ abla\!\cdot\!(p_t u_t)=0\): the averaged field transports the marginal. Because \(\mathbb{E}\|u_ heta-u_t(\cdot\mid z)\|^2\) and \(\mathbb{E}\|u_ heta-u_t\|^2\) differ by a \( heta\)-independent constant, regressing onto conditional targets recovers \(u_t\) at the minimizer. \(\square\)

In fabius. This shapes R4's "defer and average" reflex: when candidate routes disagree, fabius holds them as a weighted blend (a soft posterior over routes) and lets the integrated signal sharpen before collapsing to one — scout wide, then strike narrow as the marginal resolves.

Honesty boundary. This theorem is proven only about deterministic transport of probability densities by learned vector fields on \(\mathbb{R}^d\) — sampling math for generative models. It says nothing about agents, routes, or decisions: there is no measure \(q\), no continuity equation, and no field \(u_t\) over a discrete route set, and no claim here is validated on agent behavior. Fabius borrows only the shape — average candidates until the signal sharpens — and its honest core is its own maxim, not this identity: scout wide / strike narrow.

title: Classifier-free guidance trades breadth for adherence (analogy)
html:
Statement. Let a diffusion model at noise level \(t\) admit an unconditional score \( abla_x \log p_t(x)\) and a conditional score \( abla_x \log p_t(x\mid c)\), estimated by noise-predictors \(\epsilon(\varnothing)\) and \(\epsilon(c)\) (where \(\epsilon \propto - abla_x \log p_t\)). Classifier-free guidance (CFG) samples with the extrapolated estimate \( ilde{\epsilon} = \epsilon(\varnothing) + w\, igl(\epsilon(c) - \epsilon(\varnothing) igr)\), \(w \ge 1\). Then \( ilde{\epsilon}\) is the score of a tilted density \( ilde{p}_t(x\mid c) \propto p_t(x)\,p_t(c\mid x)^{w}\); raising \(w\) sharpens this density toward high-likelihood-of-\(c\) modes, increasing conditional adherence while shrinking variance (diversity) — a bias\(\uparrow\)/variance\(\downarrow\) trade with an empirically modest sweet spot.

Proof. By Bayes, \( abla_x \log p_t(x\mid c) = abla_x \log p_t(x) + abla_x \log p_t(c\mid x)\). Define the implicit classifier gradient \(g := abla_x \log p_t(c\mid x) = abla_x \log p_t(x\mid c) - abla_x \log p_t(x)\). The CFG combination in score form is \[ ilde{s}_w(x) = abla_x \log p_t(x) + w\, igl( abla_x \log p_t(x\mid c) - abla_x \log p_t(x) igr) = abla_x \log p_t(x) + w\,g. \] Since \( abla_x \log igl(p_t(x)\,p_t(c\mid x)^{w} igr) = abla_x \log p_t(x) + w\, abla_x \log p_t(c\mid x) = abla_x \log p_t(x) + w\,g = ilde{s}_w(x)\), the field \( ilde{s}_w\) is conservative with potential \(\log ilde p_t\), so the guided sampler targets \( ilde{p}_t(x\mid c) \propto p_t(x)\,p_t(c\mid x)^{w}\). For \(w>1\) the factor \(p_t(c\mid x)^{w}\) is a monotone-increasing convex reweighting of the likelihood: it raises mass on \(x\) with high \(p_t(c\mid x)\) and suppresses the rest, concentrating the density. Locally, near a mode the log-density Hessian is \( abla^2\log ilde p_t = abla^2\log p_t + w\, abla^2\log p_t(c\mid x)\); the added curvature from the \(w\)-weighted classifier term steepens the well, and the Laplace-approximation covariance \( igl(- abla^2\log ilde p_t igr)^{-1}\) shrinks as \(w\) grows. Hence sampled \(x\) adhere more tightly to \(c\) (bias toward typical-\(c\) modes) with lower spread (variance/diversity down). \(\square\)

In fabius. R10 governs how hard the router emphasizes an instruction/constraint when dispatching to a specialist: treat instruction emphasis like a guidance weight — turn it up to force adherence to a hard constraint, keep it modest when breadth of candidate outputs matters, and always measure both adherence and diversity rather than maxing emphasis blindly.

Honesty boundary. The result above is proven only about score-based diffusion sampling of a learned vector field, and is measured (Ho & Salimans 2022) on Inception-Score / recall trade-offs in image generation. It says nothing about prompts, instructions, or LLM agents: there is no theorem here that an "emphasis weight" on an agent instruction tilts any agent output distribution by \(p(c\mid x)^w\), because an LLM has no calibrated \(p_t(c\mid x)\) score and no diffusion sampler. fabius borrows only the shape — emphasis trades breadth for adherence. The single verifiable core claim is qualitative: pushing instruction emphasis raises adherence and lowers diversity, so measure both; the \(\propto p\cdot p(c\mid x)^w\) law and any "sweet spot" do not transfer.

title: Recency decay is a heuristic kernel, not a posterior (analogy)
html:
Statement. Fix a query \(q\) and a set \(P\) of curated wiki pages all tied on a primary relevance score, i.e. \(\mathrm{rel}(q,p)=r>0\) for every \(p\in P\). Each page carries an age \(\Delta t(p)\ge 0\) (time since last edit). Re-rank the tie by the kernel \[ w(p)\;=\;\exp\!\big(-\lambda\,\Delta t(p)\big)\cdot \mathrm{rel}(q,p),\qquad \lambda>0. \] Claim: this is a strictly monotone re-ordering in \(\Delta t\) — for \(p_1,p_2\in P\), \(\;\Delta t(p_1)<\Delta t(p_2)\iff w(p_1)>w(p_2)\). Hence the induced ranking is exactly the order "most recently edited first", and ties in \(w\) occur only on ties in \(\Delta t\).

Proof. On \(P\), \(\mathrm{rel}(q,\cdot)\equiv r\) is constant, so \(w(p)=r\,e^{-\lambda\Delta t(p)}\) with \(r>0\). Write \(w(p)=g(\Delta t(p))\) where \(g(x)=r\,e^{-\lambda x}\). Then \(g'(x)=-\lambda r\,e^{-\lambda x}<0\) for all \(x\) since \(\lambda,r>0\) and \(e^{-\lambda x}>0\); thus \(g\) is strictly decreasing on \([0,\infty)\), hence injective and order-reversing. Therefore \(\Delta t(p_1)<\Delta t(p_2)\Rightarrow g(\Delta t(p_1))>g(\Delta t(p_2))\), i.e. \(w(p_1)>w(p_2)\); and conversely \(w(p_1)>w(p_2)\Rightarrow g(\Delta t(p_1))>g(\Delta t(p_2))\Rightarrow \Delta t(p_1)<\Delta t(p_2)\) by strict monotonicity. The map \(p\mapsto w(p)\) thus reverses the total preorder by \(\Delta t\) exactly, with equal \(w\) iff equal \(\Delta t\). The value of \(\lambda>0\) and of the constant \(r\) is immaterial to the order: any \(\lambda>0\) yields the identical permutation, since strict monotonicity of \(e^{-\lambda x}\) holds for every positive rate. \(\square\)

In fabius. archivum's M8 retrieval breaks a relevance tie on a curated wiki by preferring the more recently edited page — equivalently, it applies \(w(p)=e^{-\lambda\Delta t}\mathrm{rel}\) as a deterministic recency tie-break, never as a scoring stage that can override relevance.

Honesty boundary. The exponential-decay kernel is borrowed for its shape only. The theorem above is a trivial fact about a strictly monotone scalar function; it says nothing probabilistic. In particular \(w\) is not a normalized Bayesian posterior: a genuine temporal prior would enter inside \(P(\text{relevant}\mid q,\Delta t,\dots)\) and be re-normalized over the page set, whereas \(w\) is an unnormalized heuristic that merely sorts. The source — Generative Agents (Park et al. 2023) — combines recency with a fitted decay rate \(\lambda\), an LLM-assigned importance score, and a reflection threshold counter over a stream of synthetic memories; those quantities are proven about that simulation, not about retrieval correctness or agent routing. fabius keeps only the monotone decay tie-break and deliberately drops the importance score, the threshold counter, and the fitted \(\lambda\), so no claim of optimality or posterior calibration is made or needed.
